- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque, also known as the Sultan Ahmed Mosque, was constructed between 1609 and 1616 during the reign of Sultan Ahmed I.
- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque features over 20,000 handmade ceramic tiles in shades of blue, green, and white.
- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque's tile work reflects the tradition of Turkish ceramics dating back to the 13th century, with patterns including floral and geometric designs and Quranic calligraphy.
- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque has six minarets, indicating its importance and showcasing Sultan Ahmed I's power and wealth.
- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque's calligraphy features verses from the Quran, designed to inspire spiritual reflection.
- [2023/05/25] The Blue Mosque's geometric patterns often represent infinite perfection and sacred geometry.
- [2023/05/25] Other famous Ottoman-era buildings with intricate calligraphy and patterns include Topkapi Palace, Suleymaniye Mosque, Dolmabahce Palace, and Rüstem Pasha Mosque.
- [2023/05/25] In Ottoman art and architecture, blue represents the sky and spirituality, green symbolizes life and fertility, red signifies power and wealth, and gold denotes divinity and luxury.
- [2023/05/25] The decline of the Ottoman Empire was due to military, economic, political, and social challenges, impacting its architectural and cultural legacy.
